newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina Senate approves Triad baseball vote.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina Senate approves Triad baseball vote.

text.p: The North Carolina Senate give final approval Wednesday to a May referendum allowing Forsyth and Guilford county residents to vote on a tax to finance a baseball stadium.
The Senate approved the proposal 39-10 and sent it to Gov. Jim Hunt, who has indicated he will sign it. The House approved the proposal last week.
It authorizes a May 5 referendum on a propsoal to levy a one percent tax on restaurant meals in the two counties and a 50-cent surcharge on tickets for stadium events.

Revenues would be used to pay debt service on tax-exempt, 25-year stadium bonds. If approved, the two counties would form a stadium financing authority to issue the debt and the stadium would be built on the Guilford-Forsyth County line.

Public funding for the $210 million stadium would be capped at $140 million. An investment group headed by nursing home executive Don Beaver would put up another $70 million for the stadiuma nd $150 million to buy a franchise.
The tax would only take effect if the group wins a major league baseball expansion team in 1999 or buys an existing team.
